thread.title: Microsoft’s bearish ‘death cross’ to finally appear, ahead of earnings - MarketWatch

author: Tomi Kilgore
title: Microsoft’s bearish ‘death cross’ to finally appear, ahead of earnings - MarketWatch
text:
Microsoft Corp., which climbed to the top of the heap of U.S. companies two months ago, will finally join its technology-heavyweight peers by producing a bearish “death cross” chart pattern.
Microsoft’s stock MSFT, +1.89% fell 2.0% Tuesday, adding to Monday’s 2% drop. The two-day selloff comes as investors grew cautious about the technology sector, after chip maker Nvidia Corp. NVDA, +0.36% warned of a big revenue shortfall , with Chief Executive Jensen Huang calling the fourth quarter an “extraordinary, unusually turbulent and disappointing quarter.”
See related : Nvidia suffers slew of downgrades as analysts weigh sales warning .
Microsoft’s 50-day moving average, which many chart watchers use as a guide to the shorter-term trend, fell to $104.7674 on Tuesday from Monday’s $104.8474, according to FactSet. Meanwhile, the 200-day moving average, viewed by many as a dividing line between longer-term uptrends and downtrends, rose to $104.6742 from $104.6274.
On Wednesday, the 50-DMA was on track to fall to $104.7268, according to FactSet, just a hair above the 200-DMA, which was headed for a rise to $104.7235. The sets up the appearance of “death cross” on Thursday, barring a sharp decline in Microsoft’s stock on Wednesday.
The shares rose 1.7% ahead of Wednesday’s open.
FactSet, MarketWatch Many on Wall Street believe a “death cross” marks the spot that a shorter-term pullback transitions into a longer-term downtrend.
The last time Microsoft’s 50-day moving average was below its 200-day moving average was Aug. 8, 2016, while the last “death cross” appeared on June 23, 2016.
After the last “death cross,” the stock fell 4.7% over the next two sessions, but was up 14% three months later. The one before that, the stock lost 1.7% before bottoming 6 weeks later, but was up 25.5% after three months.
Microsoft is scheduled to report fiscal second-quarter results after Wednesday’s close. The company has beat earnings expectations the past 10 quarters, according to FactSet, and beat revenue projections the past six quarters.
Don’t miss : Microsoft earnings: How to look for a clue about a cloud downturn
The stock has gained on the first trading day after earnings were reported in 15 of the past 20 quarters, by an average of 3.9%. The average of the five declines during that period was 4.3%.
Microsoft, which wrested the title of largest U.S. company by market-capitalization from Apple Inc AAPL, +3.90% in November, is the last of the large-cap tech stocks to avoid the bearish “death cross” fate.
Also read : Apple’s ‘death cross’ is first in 3 years, and last for FAANG stocks .
Here are the dates that a “death cross” appeared in the stock charts of the other tech heavyweights, and of the major market indexes.
• Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, +2.60% currently the second most valuable U.S. company: Dec. 12, 2018.
• Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOGL, +1.41% the third most valuable U.S. company: Nov. 15, 2018.
• Apple Inc. AAPL, +3.90% the fourth most valuable U.S. company: Dec. 20, 2018.
• Facebook Inc. FB, +1.57% : Sept. 20, 2018.
• Intel Corp. INTC, -0.08% : Sept. 10, 2018.
• Cisco Systems Inc. CSCO, +0.27% : Jan. 25, 2019.
• Netflix Inc. NFLX, +1.65% : Nov. 19, 2018.
• Nasdaq-100 Index NDX, +1.04% : Dec. 3, 2018.
• S&P 500 index SPX, +0.41% : Dec. 7, 2018.
• Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.92% : Dec. 19, 2018.
